messages.body_plain:
Thanks as always!

I wanted to confirm that I understood your instructions above re:
converting multiple correlation types into Fisher's z.  I have a dataframe
with adjusted beta, partial r, rho, beta, and unstandardized b.  Is this
delta correction correct? Note: r_oriented is the effect size and N_Effect
is the sample size --

meta_df_other <- meta_df %>% subset(Reported_Stat_Type != r (Pearson)")
meta_df_other <- escalc(measure = "COR", ri=r_oriented, ni=N_Effect, data =
meta_df_other)
meta_df_other <- conv.delta(yi, vi, data=meta_df_other, transf=transf.rtoz,
replace=TRUE)

messages.body_plain:
Dear Tori,

I assume variable 'r_oriented' contains the mix of regular correlations, adjusted betas, partial r's, standardized regression coefficients, and unstandardized regression coefficients. If so, then what you are doing is not correct. By feeding this variable into escalc() with measure="COR", the calculations are based on the assumption that variable 'r_oriented' ONLY contains regular Pearson product-moment correlation coefficients, which is not the case here.

Also, unstandardized regression coefficients cannot be mixed at all with correlation coefficients, as they are on entirely different scales. Same goes for standardized regression coefficients (except for the case of simple regression where the standardized regression coefficient is equal to the Pearson correlation).

Best,
Wolfgang

messages.body_plain:
Thanks, Michael. And now?!

I'm planning a small network meta-analysis and would value your
input on two design questions.


SETUP

I have three parallel-group RCTs comparing treatments A, B and C
(mean value at post per arm):

              Tx A    Tx B    Tx C
  Study I      100     150       -
  Study II     200    200      -
  Study III      -     200     200



I would like to add a fourth study (Study IV). It is a within-person
design: each participant's legs were randomized to different
treatments, so comparisons are within-group rather than
between-group. I have the post-treatment means + SD for each
condition.


QUESTION

Can Study IV be meta-analyzed together with the three parallel RCTs?

            Obs     Tx A    Tx B    Tx C
  Study I      1       100     150       -
  Study II     1       200       -     200
  Study III    1       200     200       -
  Study IV     1         -       -     180
  Study IV     2         -     170       -



Thanks a lot for your help.

Best,
Jorge

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jorge,

Much more readable!

I see no inherent problem with including study IV, but not sure why you structured it as you did. In essence, it is like this:

           Obs     Tx A    Tx B    Tx C
Study I      1       100     150       -
Study II     1       200       -     200
Study III    1       200     200       -
Study IV     1         -     170     180

But since study IV is a within-subjects design, the two means are not independent. So you would have to compute the covariance between them and include this in the V matrix. The covariance between the two means is a function of the correlation of the raw measurements for the two legs. If this is not reported, then you could use a guestimate and do a sensitivity analysis.

Best,
Wolfgang

How the data needs to be organized depends on the software you are using. If you are using rma.mv() from metafor, then it would indeed need to be in long format (for all studies), so:

Study trt  mean
I     A    100
I     B    150
II    A    200
II    C    200
...
IV    B    170
IV    C    180

and the V matrix is diagonal, except for the 2x2 block from study IV, where there is also the covariance.

Best,
Wolfgang
